message.content: {"appearance_facts": [{"location": "The map is a US choropleth where state polygons are filled with colors from a gradient scale.", "fact": "Most states are filled with light yellow, orange, or red tones, while several states (including ND, KS, NC, and KY) are filled with a dark maroon color."}, {"location": "The legend is located on the right side of the map.", "fact": "The vertical color bar ranges from light yellow at the top (labeled 'High' and 100) to dark maroon at the bottom (labeled 'Low' and 0)."}, {"location": "Kansas (KS) is in the central US.", "fact": "The KS polygon is filled with a dark maroon color, which corresponds to the 'Low' end of the legend scale."}, {"location": "Illinois (IL) is in the midwest.", "fact": "The IL polygon is filled with a light yellow color, which corresponds to the 'High' end of the legend scale."}, {"location": "Delaware (DE) is on the east coast.", "fact": "The DE polygon is filled with a dark maroon color, similar to KS."}, {"location": "Comparing the three option states (IL, KS, DE).", "fact": "KS and DE share the same dark maroon fill color, while IL has a distinctly lighter, yellow fill color."}], "printed_facts": [{"location": "Top left corner.", "fact": "Title reads 'Risk Index of Hazard H in US States'."}, {"location": "Right side legend.", "fact": "Legend title is 'High' at the top and 'Low' at the bottom."}, {"location": "Right side legend.", "fact": "Numeric scale runs from 100 at the top to 0 at the bottom, with ticks at 20, 40, 60, and 80."}, {"location": "Map labels.", "fact": "State abbreviations are printed on the polygons, including 'KS' for Kansas, 'IL' for Illinois, and 'DE' for Delaware."}], "public_definitions": [], "uncertain": []}
